summary: This note is an excerpt from a fiction book (labeled "Book 11 — part 25") set in a country schoolroom. The young teacher Miss Dearborn punishes Rebecca by making her stand by the water pail to stop the class's constant drinking, then publicly explains her reasoning. Classmates show Rebecca sympathy with small gifts, and Miss Dearborn privately admits she punished Rebecca more than she intended before the grammar lesson begins. The note also contains one unrelated sentence about Veronica seeing the painting 'Impression, Sunrise' up close in 2013.
one_line: An excerpt from a fiction book in which teacher Miss Dearborn punishes Rebecca for drinking at the water pail and then makes amends.
key_facts: Miss Dearborn asked Rebecca to stand by the pail to break up a habit of incessant drinking, which she called empty-mindedness and a desire to walk to and fro over the floor.
Every time Rebecca asked for a drink that day, the whole school went to the pail one after another.
Miss Dearborn said she ought to have punished the scholars for following Rebecca's example, not Rebecca for setting it.
Miss Dearborn was only eighteen herself and in her year of teaching country schools had never encountered a child like Rebecca.
Rebecca protested, 'I hadn't missed a question this whole day, nor whispered either,' and said she did not think she ought to be shamed just for drinking.
Miss Dearborn told Rebecca, 'You started all the others, or it seemed as if you did.'
Living Perkins dropped a piece of maple sugar in Rebecca's lap as he passed on his way to draw the map of Maine.
Alice Robinson rolled a perfectly new slate pencil over the floor with her foot until it reached Rebecca's place.
Emma Jane made a little mound of paper balls labeled "Bullets for you know who."
Rebecca called Sam Simpson 'a copycoat' and said she could not bear standing in the corner with him.
Miss Dearborn told Rebecca to take her seat and left Sam Simpson in the corner, saying Rebecca was a stranger whose actions were watched more closely.
Alice asked for 'The Old Oaken Bucket' to sing, and Miss Dearborn asked her to think of something dry instead.
Miss Dearborn's grammar lesson assigned the verb 'to be' in the potential mood, past perfect tense.
An unrelated sentence states that in 2013 Veronica finally saw the original 'Impression, Sunrise' painting up close after waiting in line for hours.
